Theme

Playground equipment, sandbox toys, vehicles and play

boxing noun

also boxer, box (verb), boxing glove, boxing match, boxing champion, heavyweight champion, boxing ring, round (boxing)

classical

Plaut. Bacch. 3.3.24
Plin. NH 8.82
Traupman 46

pugilātus, pugilātūs m.

noun, fourth declension

Other words

  • pugil, pugilis m. — boxer

    noun, third declension · classical · Traupman 46, 164

    The boxer of the Roman games (Cic., Hor.); a champion is pugilum rēx (Traupman 46).

  • pugilātiō, pugilātiōnis f.

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Leg. 2.38; Traupman 46

  • caestus, caestūs m. — boxing glove

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · Traupman 46

    The ancient boxer’s thong of leather, weighted with lead (Cic. Tusc. 2.40; Verg. A. 5.379); Traupman’s word for the glove.

Examples

  • quid prōdest multōs vincere luctātiōne vel caestū, ab īrācundiā vincī?

    what good is it to beat many at wrestling or boxing, and be beaten by anger?Sen. Ep. 88.19 (Lewis & Short s.v. luctātiō)

  • pugilum rēx

    a boxing championTraupman 46

  • pugilum rēx maximī ponderis

    the heavyweight championTraupman 46

  • suggestus pugilātōrius

    the boxing ringTraupman 46

  • congressus

    a round (in boxing)Traupman 372

See also wrestling, sport, gym.
